papers.title: Multifactorial diagnosis of drought‐induced decline in Mediterranean conifer forests
keywords: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics

essence.problem: Abstract Drought‐induced tree mortality is a complex process involving interdependent shifts in tree water, carbon and nutrient relations, alongside adjustments in growth and trait variability.
essence.design: Tree‐ring metrics, foliar carbon and oxygen stable isotopes (δ 13 C, ∆ 18 O) and elemental composition and soil properties were integrated to assess drought impact on growth ( DGIi ), intrinsic water‐use efficiency (iWUE), ∆ 18 O‐inferred stomatal conductance (G ∆18O ) and nutrient status of trees.

papers.title: Rainfall memory and spring atmospheric demand predict herbaceous biomass production in Mediterranean ecosystems
papers.recommendationReason: 重点体现导师方向与应用价值；命中“drought、prediction、experimental evidence”等信号。

essence.problem: Abstract Aboveground herbaceous biomass production in Mediterranean ecosystems is often related to precipitation amount, yet similar rainfall totals can produce contrasting biomass.
essence.design: Treatment‐specific rainfall records were combined with meteorological data and Random Forest modelling.
essence.innovation: Favourable rainfall conditions during the previous growing season were also strongly associated with greater current biomass, revealing a climatic legacy across growing seasons.

papers.title: Decoding nearly four decades of rubber plantation age in China using Bi-directional CCDC and height–age model
keywords: Plant Water Relations and Carbon Dynamics
papers.recommendationReason: 重点体现应用价值；命中“management、indicator、assessment”等信号。

essence.problem: Abstract Stand age is a key ecological and management indicator for rubber plantations, because it controls plantation productivity, renewal cycles, carbon accumulation, and tropical land-use legacies.
essence.design: In this study, we reconstructed annual 30 m stand-age maps of rubber plantations in China from 1987 to 2022 by integrating Landsat time-series analysis, an improved Bi-directional Continuous Change Detection and Classification (BCDC) algorithm, handheld laser scanning (HLS)-derived plot height, and a four-parameter logistic height-age model.

papers.title: Vegetation structure and diaspore traits shape secondary wind dispersal: wind-tunnel insights
papers.recommendationReason: 主题信号较弱，因期刊范围、时效性或方法价值进入候选，建议结合摘要判断。

essence.problem: Abstract Vegetation structure’s role in secondary wind dispersal remains poorly understood.
essence.design: We used wind-tunnel experiments with standardized, artificially constructed vegetation treatments to quantify the proportion of diaspores dispersed beyond 5 m over bare ground and through 12 vegetation treatments that varied in cover (0–30%), life-form composition, vertical arrangement and horizontal pattern.
